tools.title: ATS Jobs Scraper – Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever & More
tools.summary: Live job postings from any company's Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Recruitee, Workable, SmartRecruiters or Workday career board, normalized into one schema with location, remote status and salary where the ATS exposes it. Don't know which ATS a company uses? Leave it out and the Actor auto-detects the platform from the slug alone. Filter by title, location, department, posting-date window or a keyword in the full description text; watch mode returns only the postings that are new since your last run.
tools.description: Give it a list of companies as {"ats": "auto|greenhouse|ashby|lever|recruitee|workable|smartrecruiters|workday", "slug": "..."} and it pulls every live posting straight from each company's own career-board API — no browser, no login. Omit ats or set it to "auto" and it tries all 6 non-Workday platforms for that slug and keeps whichever one is real — you only need to know the company, not the ATS. Seven ATSes normalized into one schema — the only one of these seven to also include Recruitee. Supports titleKeyword/titleExcludeKeyword, locationKeyword/locationExcludeKeyword, hasSalary, remoteOnly and postedAfter filters applied before you're charged. Companies that have moved off an ATS (common for Lever) are skipped with a warning instead of failing the run. No start fee.

tools.title: Google News Scraper – Real URLs, Any Language
tools.summary: Search Google News by keyword, topic or publisher and get articles with the headline (raw and with the " - Publisher" suffix stripped), source name and domain, date, feed rank and the resolved publisher URL — plus related coverage of the same story and optional full article text, author, image and keywords. Any language or country.
tools.description: Supports Google News operators such as "exact phrase", site:reuters.com, when:7d and before:2026-01-01. Up to 100 articles per query. Google's encoded redirect links are resolved to the publisher's real URL. Also browse built-in sections (World, Business, Technology, Entertainment, Science, Sports, Health) with the topics field — no RSS URL needed. Restrict to a date window with timePeriod (1h … 1y) or publishedAfter/publishedBefore (YYYY-MM-DD) — Google applies the filter, so you are not charged for articles outside the window. siteFilter/excludeSites restrict or exclude publisher domains across every query with no extra requests. Optional extractTickers pulls stock tickers (e.g. $TSLA, NASDAQ:AAPL, “Tesla, Inc. (TSLA)”) into a tickers array, free.

tools.title: App Store Reviews Scraper – Any App, Any Country
tools.summary: Apple App Store reviews for any iOS or Mac App Store app and country storefront: rating, title, text, author (with profile URL), version, vote counts, sort/client diagnostics, plus full app metadata (developer, bundle id, genre, current version, store URL). Optional watch mode (watchLabel) returns only the reviews posted since your last run, so a scheduled watch on a quiet app returns nothing and costs nothing.

tools.description: Apple exposes the 500 most recent reviews per app per country (sorted by most recent or most helpful). Run on a schedule and deduplicate by reviewId to build a history.

tools.title: Shopify Products Scraper – Full Catalog, Any Store
tools.summary: Full product catalog of any Shopify store or collection: prices, compare-at prices, discount %, every variant with SKU, options, stock and image, plus tags, images, plain-text and HTML descriptions. Filter by price window (minPrice/maxPrice, matched against each product's own variant price range), discount depth (onSaleOnly/minDiscountPercent), brand or product type (vendors/productTypes, OR-matched lists) or keyword before any row is charged. Optional Apify Proxy routing for rate-limited or geo-priced stores. Optional detailLevel:"full" adds each product's SEO title/description, star-rating summary, per-variant quantity rules (min/max/case-pack) and subscription plans (one extra request/product, priced separately).
tools.description: Works on any Shopify storefront without login. Pass a store homepage for the whole catalog, a /collections/<handle> URL for one collection, or a /products/<handle> URL for a single product.

tools.title: Hacker News Scraper – Stories, Comments, Jobs, Who's Hiring
tools.summary: Search or browse Hacker News stories, comments, Ask HN, Show HN and Who's Hiring threads via the official Algolia API, with points, date and exclude-keyword filters. Watch mode returns only what's new since your last run. Optional GitHub enrichment adds stars, language and last-push date for any linked repo.

sample_output.title: Show HN: Apify – Turn any website into an API

tools.description: Uses HN's official Algolia Search API, so results are fast and reliable. Filter by tag (story, comment, ask_hn, show_hn, job), minimum points, date range, and excludeKeywords to drop off-topic matches HN's search can't exclude server-side. Leave queries empty and sort by date to pull the newest items for a tag, e.g. the latest monthly Who's Hiring thread. Optional enrichGithubLinks adds star count, language and last-push date for any linked GitHub repo.

tools.title: Google Play Reviews Scraper – Rating, Keyword & Date Filters
tools.summary: Google Play app reviews and full app metadata by app ID or search term: review rating, text, date, version, reviewer name and profile photo, developer replies and per-aspect sub-ratings, plus the app's score, ratings and review counts, install range, price and currency, genre, content rating, and release/last-updated dates. Optional watch mode (watchLabel) returns only the reviews posted since your last run, so a scheduled watch on a quiet app returns nothing and costs nothing.
tools.description: Pass Google Play package names (appIds, e.g. com.spotify.music) or plain searchTerms to resolve the top matching app automatically. Returns review rows plus an optional app-details row (installs, score, rating histogram, developer). Supports country/language targeting and sort by newest, rating or helpfulness.

tools.title: Substack Scraper – Posts, Full Text & Comments
tools.summary: Any Substack publication as structured data: posts with full article text, engagement stats (reactions, comments, restacks), podcast episodes with duration, section and cover image, plus threaded comments. Optional publication profile — subscriber count, subscription plan prices, author and bestseller tier. Custom domains supported.

Reads only what a logged-out visitor sees: no login, no paywall bypass, no headless browser.

tools.title: Apple Podcasts Scraper – Episodes, Reviews, Charts & Publishers
tools.summary: Apple Podcasts as structured data: every episode with direct audio URL, duration and RSS feed; listener reviews with star ratings; keyword search; or Apple's top-shows and trending-episodes charts. Any country storefront.

tools.description: Five modes in one Actor. episodes returns every episode of a show with its direct audio file URL (episodeUrl), duration, publish date, description and the show's RSS feed. reviews returns listener reviews with star rating, title, body, author and date, filterable by minRating/maxRating and by keyword. podcasts searches Apple Podcasts by keyword and can be chained straight into episodes or reviews. charts pulls Apple's Top Shows chart (overall or by genre) or its separate Trending Episodes chart, and publisher lists every show one publisher runs. Accepts an Apple Podcasts URL, a bare collection ID or a search term, in any country storefront. HTTP-only: no login, no headless browser.

tools.title: Steam Reviews Scraper – Playtime, Keyword & Language Filters
tools.summary: Steam player reviews as structured data: full review text, reviewer playtime, thumbs up/down, helpfulness votes and purchase type — plus a games mode with prices, genres, developers, review-score summaries, live player counts and optional SteamSpy owner estimates, peak concurrent players and crowd-voted tags. Optional watch mode (watchLabel) returns only the reviews posted since your last run, so a scheduled watch on a quiet game returns nothing and costs nothing.

sample_output.review: Best roguelike I have ever played, and the story actually lands.

tools.description: Two modes in one Actor. reviews returns Steam player reviews with the full text, the reviewer's playtime at review and total, whether they recommend the game, helpfulness votes, comment count and whether it was a genuine Steam purchase — filterable by language, reviewType (positive/negative), purchaseType, minPlaytimeHours and a text keyword. Set includeOffTopic to also return the reviews Steam hides when Valve flags a stretch of time as an off-topic review bomb — 94,228 reviews for Total War: ROME II instead of 88,334. games returns the store record for each game: price and discount in any country's currency, release date, developers, publishers, genres, platforms, Metacritic score, the full review-score summary (total positive/negative and % positive) and optionally the live concurrent player count. Accepts Steam store URLs, numeric App IDs or plain game names to search. HTTP-only: no login, no API key, no headless browser.

tools.title: Scholarship Scraper (bold.org)
tools.summary: Scholarship listings from bold.org as structured data: award amount, number of awards, deadline, essay prompt, judging criteria, education levels, donor and the live applicant count — plus a computed applicants-per-award competitiveness ratio.
tools.notice: Currently blocked: bold.org has put its entire site behind bot-protection that returns an error before any page loads. Runs fail fast and are not charged. We re-check nightly and will remove this notice the moment it clears.

sample_output.name: Pamela Branchini Memorial Scholarship
sample_output.donorName: Dan Branchini and the Glitter Team at Community Lutheran

tools.description:
Every scholarship listed on bold.org as a clean row: the award amount and how many awards are given, the deadline (with rolling deadlines flagged), the actual essay question as plain text with its word limits, the judging criteria, which education levels can apply, the donor, and bold.org's live applicant count. From those last two numbers we compute applicantsPerAward, so you can rank a list by how winnable each award actually is rather than by headline dollar amount.

Crawls the by-major, by-state, by-type, by-demographics and by-year category families (discovered from bold.org's own sitemap — never a query-string URL, which its robots.txt disallows), returning about 30 complete records per HTTP request and de-duplicating across categories. Filter by minimum award, deadline window, education level, or open-only. HTTP-only: no login, no headless browser, no proxy.

tools.title: EU TED Tenders Scraper – Country, CPV, Date & Expert Query
tools.summary: EU public-procurement notices from TED (Tenders Electronic Daily), the EU's official journal: buyer name and contact, contract value, CPV codes, place of performance, deadlines and notice link, normalized from TED's raw multilingual/duplicated-array format into flat English-preferred JSON. Filter by country, CPV code, notice type, procedure type (open/restricted/negotiated), full-text keywords, contract value range (minValue/maxValue), submission-deadline window (onlyOpenDeadlines / minDaysUntilDeadline, so you only get tenders you can still bid on) or an absolute publication-date window. Optional watch mode (watchLabel) delivers only notices new since your last run, and an optional flatten mode joins the array fields into comma-separated strings for clean CSV/Excel export. Every notice carries a procedureIdentifier shared with its corrigenda, plus changeReasonDescription — TED's own plain-text explanation of what changed — on corrigendum notices.

tools.title: ClinicalTrials.gov Scraper – Condition, Phase & Site Mode
tools.summary: Scrape ClinicalTrials.gov's official NIH API: condition, intervention, sponsor, location, facility and lead-sponsor filters, plus six date windows (start, completion, first-posted, results). Optional one-row-per-site mode for site-selection buyers. Eligibility-age bounds accept months, weeks or days as well as whole years, so neonatal and paediatric searches land. No contact people, phones or emails shipped, ever. Optional watchLabel mode returns only studies new since your last run, so a schedule becomes a trial alert; add watchChanges to also catch status changes, protocol/enrollment updates and completion-date slips on studies you already got.

Optional watchLabel mode returns only opportunities new since your last run, so a schedule becomes a grant alert; add watchChanges to also catch deadline extensions, status changes and forecasts turning into real posted opportunities.

tools.title: NIH RePORTER Grants Scraper – No 15k Row Cap
tools.summary: Search NIH-funded research projects via the official NIH RePORTER API: keyword, fiscal year, institute, activity code, organization, state, PI, award-amount and award-notice-date filters, plus an optional PubMed join. Auto-chunks past the API's 15,000-row wall. Watch mode returns only what's new since your last run; add watchChanges to also catch a no-cost extension, an administrative supplement, or a project ending on a project you already got.

tools.title: FEC Campaign Finance Scraper - Candidates, Donors & Spending
tools.summary: Search US federal candidates (House, Senate, President) by name, state, office, party and election cycle via the FEC's official open.fec.gov API, with each candidate's campaign financial totals (receipts, disbursements, cash on hand, individual contributions) included. Three transaction modes cover the money itself: donor contributions (Schedule A) by donor name, employer, occupation, city or ZIP code, committee spending (Schedule B) by vendor/recipient, and independent expenditures (Schedule E) for or against a named candidate. No API key needed, no login required. Optional watch mode (watchLabel) delivers only rows new since your last run in any transaction mode.

tools.title: Court Records & Case Law Scraper — Dockets + Opinions
tools.summary: Search US federal court dockets (the free PACER/RECAP mirror) and published court opinions through CourtListener's public API — no API key, no registration, no login. Dockets return parties, attorneys, law firms, assigned judge, nature of suit, cause of action, jurisdiction type, bankruptcy chapter and per-filing entries with a direct PDF link and the filing's OCR'd text where RECAP has it; opinions return reported citations, cite count, judge and panel, status and an opinion snippet, with an opinionStatus filter (published/unpublished/any — the default silently drops ~1 in 4 real matches unless set to 'any'). Both indexes come back in one unified schema. Server-side field searches — partyName, attorneyName, docketNumber and judge — narrow by who is on a case or by case number instead of relying on full text, and are only ever sent to the index that actually carries the field. Sort by filing date (newest or oldest first) or leave it at relevance. Optional watch mode (watchLabel) delivers only records new since your last run.
